Klean by Geerho Super Admin Manual

For laundromat business owners and managers. A Super Admin runs one Klean business ("operator"): prices, branches, machines, staff, reports and customers.

1. Switch on operator mode

Your business runs on your personal, verified Klean account. There's no separate business login.

  1. Sign in and complete identity verification.
  2. Account → Start a laundromat business in the app, or on klean.ph/account.html. Enter the business name and country, and pick the time zone from the menu (or tap 📍 Locate me to use where you are now). Reports and daily payouts follow it. Currency is set automatically for the Philippines (PHP) and fixed once created.
  3. A Business tab appears. You're the Super Admin.

1a. Beta testing (on until you go live)

Every business starts with Business → Setup → Beta testing switched on:

  • Payments use test money: nobody is charged and nothing is paid out.
  • Simulated machines from Klean HQ work, so you can try every step with your phone.
  • Delete beta test data… clears test orders, test customers and their points. Branches, machines, staff and settings stay.

To take real payments, switch Beta off. You need: Klean launched (Klean switches real payments on), your payout account set up, and at least one real washer or dryer connected with a Klean controller and online. Going live deletes all beta data and switches simulated machines off. You can turn Beta back on later; your real sales records are kept.

2. Get paid: connect payouts

Business → Setup → Payments. You can't take payments until your payout account is ready.

  • Philippines, personal account: choose your GCash, Maya or bank account and enter the account number. The account must be in your own verified name (the name on the ID you verified with). Payments switch on immediately.
  • Philippines, business account: tap Business bank account (company name)…. Enter the registered business name, whether it's registered with DTI, SEC or CDA, the registration number, the bank and account number (the account name must match the business name), and add a clear photo or PDF of the registration certificate. Klean checks it, usually within a day, and you get a notification. Until it's approved, payouts keep going to your current account (a new business can't take payments until one account is ready). If it's declined, the reason shows under Payments; fix it and send it again. Saving a personal account later switches payouts back to it.
  • Everywhere else (Stripe): tap Connect payouts and finish Stripe's short sign-up. Payments switch on as soon as Stripe confirms your account.

How the money flows

Customers pay Klean (through PayMongo or Stripe). Every day around 2:00 a.m. (Manila time), Klean automatically pays your business its share of the previous day's payments:

your payout = sales − Klean commission − payment-processor fees − transfer fee

  • The commission rate is shown on the Setup screen. Processor fees (PayMongo's fee for each GCash/Maya/card payment, or Stripe's) are passed on at cost. In the Philippines the transfer to your account costs ₱10 per daily payout.
  • Payouts under ₱100 (US$5) wait until the next day. A failed payout (e.g. a closed account) is retried after you fix the account; you'll get a notification.
  • Free loads redeemed with points carry no commission and no payout.
  • Cash sales (recorded at the counter) are already in your drawer, so they aren't paid out; their commission (same rate) comes off your next payout of digital payments instead. A cash refund you hand back gives you back that commission in the next payout.

The commission rate is set by Klean, not by you, and isn't editable from your dashboard. Every order records the rate it was charged at, so a future change never affects past orders. Klean may give your business its own rate: a lower rate starts with your next payment, and any increase starts at least 30 days after you're told. You get a notification either way, and the Setup screen shows the date of a change that's coming.

Klean is free to download and free to set up. There's no subscription. Klean earns only when you do.

3. Prices, loads and loyalty

Business → Setup → Pricing & loyalty.

SettingDefaultNotes
Price per load (wash + dry)₱250 (PH)New orders only; orders in progress keep their price
Wash only₱175 (PH)Leave blank to not offer it
Dry only₱199 (PH)Leave blank to not offer it
Max kg per load8 kgLoads = weight ÷ max, rounded up
1 point perprice ÷ 10 (₱25)So customers earn 10 points per paid load
Points for a free wash + dry100"Buy 10, get the 11th free"
Welcome bonus10On a customer's first paid visit to your business
Points expire after12 months

Customers choose wash + dry, wash only or dry only (only the services you price). A dry-only load is what a customer gets when they scan a dryer with nothing saved. Every service shows on your public laundromat page.

Customers scanning a machine can pay for up to 5 loads at once (never more than the branch's washers): the scanned washer starts and the rest are saved in their wallet for 30 days. It's one order and one payment in your reports, with the loads counted; points and commission follow the amount paid.

The screen previews the effect ("free load after about 10 paid loads"). Points belong to your business: earned at any of your branches, redeemable at any of your branches, never anywhere else. You fund the free loads, so set these numbers deliberately.

Welcome load (off by default): switch it on and brand-new Klean members get their first wash + dry free at your laundromat: people verified in the last 30 days who haven't done laundry anywhere on Klean yet. Each person gets one welcome load across all of Klean, at the first participating laundromat they scan; their machine starts without payment and they get a "Welcome to …" notification. It's your promotion: no payment, no commission, no payout.

3a. What you offer: laundromat, carwash, motorcycle wash

When you create the business you choose what it offers; change it in Business → Setup → What you offer: Laundromat (washers and dryers), Carwash: self-service bays, Carwash: full service, Motorcycle wash: self-service bays, or all of them. Klean shows only the screens that apply (for example Work → Intake for laundromats, Work → Carwash for full service).

  • Self-service bays (Setup → Self-service wash bays): set a price for a block of minutes for car bays and for motorcycle bays (e.g. ₱50 for 5 minutes). Customers scan the bay, pay for 1–12 blocks, start the bay, and tap Add time while it runs. Add bays in Klean HQ (set up a location → Car wash bays / Motorcycle wash bays) like machines; each gets its own QR code and status light. With a Klean controller, a bay's pulses setting is coins per minute: Klean drops minutes paid × that many coins, and more on Add time. Bench-test a controller on one bay before installing (the bay firmware is new as of 2026-10-22).
  • Full service (Setup → Full-service menu): add services (e.g. Wash, Wash + Wax, Interior) with a price per vehicle size (Motorcycle, Sedan, SUV, Van / Pickup; blank = not offered for that size). Attendants ring them up in Work → Carwash and move each car through Waiting → Washing → Done → Picked up; Done tells a customer with a Klean account their vehicle is ready.
  • You're responsible for bay equipment, water, chemicals, drainage and any environmental permits, signs and safety.

4. Branches and machines

Add a branch: Business → Setup → Branches → + Add a branch. One form: the branch's name and address (📍 Use my current location or Find address puts it on the map), a contact phone and email (shown to customers), how many washers and dryers with their cycle minutes and brand/model, and whether a weigh scale is connected. Klean creates the machines labelled W1, W2… and D1, D2…, each with its QR code.

Manage a branch: tap it to edit its details or map position, and to manage its machines: + Add washer / + Add dryer (the next label, like W6), Rename a label, show a machine's QR code to print, or Delete a machine, or Write NFC sticker (Android: NFC) to put a tap-to-pay sticker beside its QR (Hardware Guide → NFC tap stickers). A machine that has never been used is deleted; one that has is retired (its QR stops working, it disappears from lists, its history stays). Machines can't be deleted while paid, held or running.

Deleting a branch: Business → Setup → Branches → Delete branch…, type its name. Klean approves each request (you'll get a notification). A branch that never had a sale is deleted with its machines; one with sales is closed instead: its machines stop, customers no longer see it, and its sales stay in your reports. It can't happen while a machine there is paid, held or running.

Put each branch on the map so customers find it: Business → Setup → Branches. Standing inside the laundromat, tap 📍 Use my current location; or tap Find address on map to use the branch's address. Customers then see it under Laundromats near you with live free machines and directions. (Beta laundromats show only to their testers until you go live.)

Klean HQ (on a computer) is the easiest way to set up a location: it asks how many washers and dryers you have, creates them all with their QR codes, and shows each machine's live light (green available, white paid and waiting for Start, blue in use, red error). Machines can be Real (a Klean controller is installed) or Simulated (Klean HQ plays the machine, so you can try everything before installing hardware). Its Hardware page lists what to buy or build, how it connects, and gives you the controller file to flash. Full details: the Hardware Guide.

Machines never start by themselves (real or simulated). After paying, the customer taps Start wash / Start dry in Klean (after confirming the laundry is in and the door is closed) or presses Start on the machine; on a simulated machine you can also click Press Start in Klean HQ. If your machines start as soon as coins go in, tick that box before downloading the controller file, so Klean holds the coins until the customer taps Start.

Testing in Beta: reset simulated machines. If a simulated machine gets stuck (for example paid and waiting for a Start that never comes), click Reset on it in Klean HQ, or Reset all simulated machines; in the app or on klean.ph it's Work → Machines → Reset simulated machines (Beta). The machine goes back to Available and any load waiting to start goes back to its order (find it under Work → Intake → Paid, still to start). Only simulated machines in a Beta business can be reset; real machines and live businesses are never touched.

In the app:

  1. Setup → Branches → Add branch for each location.
  2. Install a Klean controller box for the machines (wired to the coin input; see the Hardware Guide).
  3. Setup → Add a machine: choose the branch and type, and enter the label painted on the machine (W1, D3…). Leave Controller ID empty and Klean creates one; enter your own only if your controller box came with an ID.
  4. A QR code appears. Print it and stick it on the machine at eye level. Customers scan it to pay.
  5. If a sticker is ever copied or damaged, rotate the machine's QR (old stickers stop working).

Klean Scale (optional)

A Klean Scale sends each settled weight to Klean, so customers don't type it (and can't under-weigh). Business → Setup → Branches → the branch → Klean Scale → + Add a Klean Scale. In Beta it's simulated: weigh things in Klean HQ (klean.ph/hq → the branch → Klean Scale → type kilos → Put on scale). For a real scale, the app shows its Controller ID and Secret once: put them in the scale's firmware (Hardware Guide → Klean Scale).

Customers tap Use the Klean Scale in Start laundry; the newest weighing from the last 2 minutes fills in, and each weighing is used once. Attendants get the same Use the Klean Scale button in Work → Intake. Require the scale (whole business) stops typed weights at every branch of your business (in Start laundry and at the counter) (customers can still choose a number of loads only if Require is off). Each branch card shows the scale's last weight. You're responsible for the scale's accuracy and, in the Philippines, for having it tested and sealed by your city or municipal treasurer (Terms 4.4d).

5. Staff

Business → Staff.

Hire

  1. Your new hire installs Klean, signs in and verifies their identity (required; they pay their own fee).
  2. They give you the member code from their Account screen.
  3. Enter it under Hire someone, choose a role, and choose their branches: - Attendant: works the POS and machine dashboard. Assign one, several, or all branches ("all" includes branches you open later). - Super Admin: full access to your business, like you.
  4. Add to team. Their own account gains staff access immediately.

Reassign, promote, remove

Tap Edit next to a team member to move them between branches, change their role, or remove them from the team. Changes apply on their next action. A business always needs at least one Super Admin.

You'll see each staff member's verified legal name, so you know exactly who works for you.

6. Sales reports

Business → Sales. Choose a period:

PeriodCovers
DailyOne calendar day (hourly chart)
WeeklyMonday to Sunday
Semi-monthly1st–15th, or 16th–end of month
MonthlyCalendar month
QuarterlyJan–Mar, Apr–Jun, Jul–Sep, Oct–Dec
Semi-annualJan–Jun or Jul–Dec
AnnualCalendar year

Use ‹ Prev / Next › to move between periods. Each report shows:

  • Gross sales, with % change vs. the previous period
  • Net to you (after Klean commission and refunds, before processor fees) and Klean commission
  • Refunds made in the period (counted on the day you refunded, like a bank statement), with net sales = gross − refunds; Klean's commission on a refund is given back, so Net to you only drops by the rest
  • Orders, average ticket, paid loads, free (points) loads, new customers
  • Sales over time, by branch, and by payment method
  • Export CSV for your accountant (amounts in centavos/cents), including refunds, net sales and the commission returned, per time bucket and per branch

All times are in your business's time zone.

6a. Orders and refunds

Business → Sales → Orders and refunds (on klean.ph: Account → Orders and refunds) lists your paid orders, newest first. Search by member code, customer name, or the order number (#1A2B3C4D).

To refund: tap Refund… on the order, choose how many loads (up to the loads not yet refunded), write a short reason (the customer sees it), and confirm. Rules:

  • Only Super Admins can refund; attendants send customers to you.
  • Up to 90 days after payment, some or all loads. A load running on a machine right now can't be cancelled (wait until it finishes); refunding a load that was used (for example after a machine fault) is allowed.
  • The money goes back to the customer's payment method through PayMongo/Stripe. Most refunds finish at once; some show processing for a while.
  • The refunded loads' unused washes/dries are cancelled, and the points that order earned are taken back in proportion.
  • Your payout: the refund minus Klean's commission on it (Klean returns its commission) comes off your next payout. The processor's fee on the original payment isn't returned. Payout statements show the refunds.
  • Beta (test) orders refund test money only.

Chargebacks (bank disputes): if a customer disputes a payment with their bank, you and Klean get a notification ("A customer disputed a payment") with the order number. Within 5 days, email Klean anything that shows the service was given: photos, messages with the customer, the machine's start and finish times. Klean answers the bank. If the bank sides with the customer, it's handled like a full refund of that order (its refund reason starts with "Chargeback", and it counts as a refund in your reports), and you're told "Dispute lost"; if it sides with you, nothing changes ("Dispute won").

6b. Cash at the counter

Customers who don't use GCash, Maya or a card can pay cash at the counter. In Work → Intake, type the weight, then tap Cash (or, after Charge, Paying cash instead); the attendant optionally types the amount handed over (Klean shows the change), and taps Cash received. Only then do the loads become paid and machines can be assigned: entering the sale in Klean is the only way a cash load gets a machine, so cash that isn't rung up can't run a wash.

A counter computer or tablet. Work is also on klean.ph → Account → Work (Machines, Intake with the payment QR or cash, Pickup), so a laptop or tablet at the counter can be the till without the app.

Starting a counter order's machines. After tapping a free washer for the order, wait for its white light, then tap Start wash on it (in Work → Intake, or on its tile in Work → Machines) and confirm the laundry is in and the door is closed. Walk-ins have no app, so staff start counter orders; machines paid in a customer's own app are started by the customer.

Every cash payment records who took it and when. Business → Sales → Cash by person (and klean.ph → Account → Expenses and cash) shows cash taken per branch and person for the day, week, month or year: count the drawer against it at the end of each shift. Attendants see their own cash for today in Work. Refunds of cash orders work like any refund (6a), but you hand the money back in cash; Klean doesn't send it anywhere.

End-of-shift count. At the end of a shift, the attendant taps Work → Intake → Count my cash and close my shift, counts the cash they took since their last count, and enters it. It's a blind count: they don't see what Klean expects until they've entered it. Any difference notifies you ("Cash short at Main St"), and every count is listed under Business → Sales → Shift counts.

Commission on cash sales. Cash stays in your drawer, so Klean's commission on it comes off your next payout of GCash, Maya and card sales. Business → Sales → Commission on cash sales shows what's owed. If you take mostly cash, tap Pay to pay it with GCash, Maya or card. If any of it is unpaid for 30 days, recording cash at the counter pauses until it's paid (digital payments keep working); you're reminded 7 days before and on the day.

6c. Expenses and profit

Business → Expenses (or klean.ph → Account → Expenses and cash). Tap Add an expense: category (utilities, detergent and soap, rent, repairs, wages, supplies, equipment, fees and permits, other), amount, date, optional branch and note. Pick a period to see:

  • Expenses by category and each item (delete a wrong one; Klean keeps a record of it). Add a photo or PDF of the receipt when you log it; tap Receipt on an item to see it. Only Super Admins can.
  • Net to you: all sales, cash included, after Klean's commission and refunds.
  • Profit = net to you − expenses.
  • Cash sales in the period, for the drawer.

Only Super Admins see or log expenses. They're your own bookkeeping; Klean doesn't check them, and they aren't official receipts or tax filings.

6d. Supplies

Work → Supplies (pick the branch). Tap Add a supply: name (Detergent, Softener, Bleach, Bags…), unit (L, kg, pcs), how much you have, Remind when down to, and optionally how much one wash or one dry uses. When set, Klean takes that off every time a cycle starts. Staff tap Record… to log a restock, what they used, or a fresh count. When a supply reaches its level, the branch's staff and you get one reminder; the next one comes after it's restocked.

6e. Maintenance

Work → Maintenance. Due now lists each machine's routine tasks that are due; staff tap Done. Tap a machine to log a repair or note or see its history (useful for warranty claims). Every business starts with three routine tasks, which you can change under Routine tasks:

  • Clean the lint filter: dryers, every 10 cycles
  • Clean the drum and door seal: washers, every 7 days
  • Check hoses, drains and vents: all machines, every 30 days

At 8 a.m. (your time zone), the staff of a branch with something due get one reminder.

6f. Receipts

Every paid order has a receipt. Customers find theirs in Account → Receipts. For a walk-in who wants one, open Business → Sales → Orders and refunds → Receipt (or on klean.ph, Account → Orders and refunds → Receipt) and print or share it. It isn't a BIR official receipt; issue official receipts as the law requires.

7. Customers

Business → Customers.

  • New sign-ups: people whose first visit to your business falls in the selected period, with a chart.
  • Active customers: people who used your laundromats in the period.
  • When customers start machines: a weekday × hour heatmap, useful for staffing and off-peak promos.
  • Loyalty ranking: your top customers by lifetime points earned at your business.
  • All customers: search by name or email; sort by last visit, newest, points or spend. Tap a customer for their points history (every earn, bonus, redemption and expiry) and usage timeline (scans, payments, cycle start/finish times).

For privacy, you see customers' display names and a masked email, never their ID documents or legal names.

7a. Messages and announcements

  • Customer messages: Business (and Work for attendants) → Customer messages. Customers write from your laundromat's page; every Super Admin and attendant is notified and can reply. Keep replies about laundry; never ask for passwords, card or ID numbers (Terms 6.1).
  • Laundry updates: when a wash or dry finishes, or laundry is marked ready for pickup, Klean posts the update in the customer's chat with your business, so their reply ("I'm on my way") reaches your staff in Customer messages.
  • Announcements: Business → Announcements → title and message → Post. Everyone who used your laundromat in the last 90 days gets a notification and sees it on Home for 30 days. Up to 3 a day; delete one any time.

8. Internet is required

Klean is online-only, on every device: phones, tablets and computers. Payments (and Klean's commission on them) are processed live, so when a device loses internet the app locks until it reconnects, with instructions to join Wi-Fi or turn on mobile data (or connect the laptop/PC to the internet). Plan for it:

  • Give each branch reliable Wi-Fi, ideally with a mobile-data backup router.
  • Machine controllers need Wi-Fi too. A controller that's offline shows red on the dashboard.

9. Your responsibilities

  • Keep machines safe and working; respond to red machines promptly.
  • Issue official receipts as required by your tax authority (in the Philippines, BIR).
  • Honor free loads earned at your business.
  • Use customer data only to run your laundromat, in line with the Privacy Policy and local law.
  • Don't take payments for Klean machines outside Klean.

10. Closing or deleting your business

Business → Setup, at the bottom (or klean.ph/account.html). Type the business name to confirm.

  • Still in Beta: Delete business removes it completely: branches, machines, staff, test orders and customers' points at your business. Everyone keeps their Klean account.
  • Taking real payments: Close business switches off your machines, removes your staff's access and takes the business off Klean. Payment records are kept as the law requires. You can close once no customer has unused paid loads with you (they last 30 days, or ask Klean Support to help refund them), your last payout has arrived, and no payment is in progress. Customers' points and free loads at your business end.
Keep it simple. Keep it Klean.
No mess. No stress. Just spotless.
